stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: For decades, many track coaches held that a long session of static stretching just before a race would help sprinters run faster. When exercise physiologists timed 40 trained sprinters over 60 meters, however, the athletes who had stretched beforehand ran slightly slower on average than those who had not. These results ______ the coaches' long-standing belief.
explanation: The coaches believed stretching makes sprinters faster, but after the word "however" the study found that sprinters who stretched ran slower. That evidence goes against the belief, so the results "challenge" it.

B.why: You picked a neutral word that sounds like research. The results don't "reveal" the coaches' belief, because the passage already stated it. The blank needs a word that says whether the evidence agrees or disagrees with the belief, and "reveal" says neither.

C.why: You missed the "however." To "repeat" the belief, the results would have to say the same thing the coaches said. Instead they show the opposite: sprinters who stretched were slower.

D.why: "Celebrate" is approving, as if the study praised the coaches' view. The slower times work against that view, so the sentence calls for disagreement, not praise.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Nutrition researchers had long suspected that eating breakfast helps schoolchildren concentrate during morning lessons. To test the idea, a team surveyed the eating habits of 600 students and gave each student a short attention test before lunch. The survey ______ the researchers' suspicion: students who had eaten breakfast scored noticeably higher on the attention test than students who had skipped it.
explanation: The researchers suspected that breakfast helps concentration. After the colon, the data show that breakfast eaters scored higher on attention, which is exactly what the researchers suspected. Evidence that agrees with a view "supported" it.

A.why: You chose a neutral verb that sounds like research. A survey doesn't "inspect" a suspicion. Also, "inspected" doesn't tell you whether the data agreed with the idea, and that is what the colon goes on to show.

B.why: You mixed up the direction of the evidence. The higher scores of breakfast eaters agree with the suspicion. They give no reason to doubt it.

C.why: To abandon a suspicion is to give it up, which researchers would do only if the evidence went against it. Here the evidence matches what they expected.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Because it contains so few stars, a faint dwarf galaxy near the Milky Way was assumed by many astronomers to hold almost no dark matter. New measurements of how quickly those stars orbit the galaxy's center, however, ______ that assumption: the stars are moving far faster than the gravity of the galaxy's visible matter alone could explain.
explanation: The astronomers assumed there was almost no dark matter. The word "however" and the finding of stars moving faster than visible matter can explain both point to hidden mass, which goes against the assumption. The measurements "undermined" it.

A.why: You were drawn to a word that sounds like astronomy. Astronomers observe stars, but measurements don't "observe" an assumption. The word also doesn't say whether the new data agreed or disagreed with the assumption.

B.why: You missed the "however." Stars moving too fast for the visible matter suggest extra unseen mass. That weakens the assumption of little dark matter. It doesn't reinforce it.

D.why: To "anticipate" an assumption would mean the measurements expected it or came before it. The measurements came later and conflict with the assumption, so this word reverses the relationship.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Because a set of nineteenth-century woodblock prints share a distinctive style of carved line, art historians had long ______ that all of them were produced in a single workshop. A recent analysis of the paper the prints were made on complicates this picture, however. The sheets came from at least three different mills, and they were made decades apart.
explanation: The blank describes the historians, not the new evidence. Because the prints share a style, the historians took it for granted that one workshop made them, and the paper analysis later complicates that view. The historians "assumed" it.

A.why: You mixed up who did what. The paper analysis questions the single-workshop idea. The historians held that idea because the prints share a style.

C.why: The historians didn't disprove the single-workshop idea. They believed it, as the cause clause "Because… share a distinctive style" shows. The paper analysis is what later complicates it.

D.why: You picked a neutral word that sounds like research. Historians may examine prints, but you don't "examine that" a claim is true. The sentence needs a word for holding a belief.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: When the city replaced the asphalt on Harmon Street with porous pavement, which lets rainwater drain into the soil below, its engineers predicted that the street would flood far less often after heavy storms. Two years of rainfall and drainage records now ______ that prediction: the amount of standing water measured on the street after storms has dropped by nearly 70 percent.
explanation: The engineers predicted less flooding. After the colon, the records show standing water down by nearly 70 percent, which is what they predicted. Evidence that shows a prediction was right "confirms" it.

A.why: You reversed the direction of the evidence. A 70 percent drop in standing water is the result the engineers predicted, so the records agree with the prediction.

B.why: You picked a neutral verb. The records don't "describe" the engineers' prediction. They describe what happened to the water. The blank needs to say how that result relates to the prediction, and "describe" doesn't.

D.why: To "predate" something is to come before it. The engineers made the prediction first and the two years of records came afterward, so this gets the order backward.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Before the region raised its minimum wage, some economists worried that restaurant owners would respond by cutting jobs to keep their labor costs down. A study that tracked staffing at 900 restaurants for three years after the increase, however, ______ this concern: employment at the restaurants stayed essentially unchanged over the whole period.
explanation: The concern was that the higher wage would cost jobs. The study, introduced by "however," found that employment barely changed. Evidence that weakens a worry "undercuts" it.

B.why: You mixed up who held the view. The economists shared the concern. The study's finding of steady employment works against the concern.

C.why: You picked a neutral word that sounds like research. The study recorded staffing numbers, not the economists' concern. "Recorded" also doesn't say whether the data supported or weakened the worry.

D.why: Steady employment gives less reason to worry about job losses, not more. To "heighten" the concern, the study would have needed to find job cuts.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: When city planners proposed building protected bike lanes along four downtown streets, they expected that the safer lanes would draw many more people to cycle into the city center. Traffic counts taken one year after the lanes opened ______ that expectation, showing that daily bike trips on the redesigned streets had more than doubled.
explanation: The planners expected more cycling, and the counts show bike trips more than doubled. The evidence shows the expectation was correct, so the counts "validated" it.

A.why: You reversed the evidence. A doubling of bike trips is what the planners expected, so the counts back up the expectation. They don't overturn it.

C.why: You picked a neutral word that sounds like research. Planners survey streets and riders, but counts don't "survey" an expectation. The word also doesn't say whether the numbers matched what the planners predicted.

D.why: "Regretted" expresses an attitude that only people can have, and it is a negative one. The data can't regret anything, and the outcome was good for the planners' expectation.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: When ecologist Ana Ruiz proposed that wolves returning to a mountain valley would help its streamside willow trees recover, many of her colleagues were ______: they doubted that a predator could influence plant life so directly. A decade of field surveys has since shown willow cover along the valley's streams nearly tripling as wolves kept browsing elk on the move.
explanation: The blank describes the colleagues, and the text after the colon defines it: they "doubted" Ruiz's idea. People who doubt a claim are "skeptical."

A.why: You mixed up who held which view. The later surveys support Ruiz, but at the time her colleagues doubted her. That is the opposite of being convinced.

B.why: You picked a word that fits the topic, since field ecologists are observant. But the text after the colon is about the colleagues' reaction to Ruiz's idea, which was doubt, and "observant" says nothing about that.

C.why: "Grateful" is a positive attitude toward the proposal. The colon explains that the colleagues doubted it, so the sentence calls for a doubting attitude, not an appreciative one.
